summary:
We developed Lunar Horizon (Lunar Landing Navigator), an interactive web-based mission planning and ephemeris simulator built for evaluating lunar landing sites. The application lets users compare key targets—including the Shackleton Crater Rim, Mare Tranquillitatis, and Tycho Crater—or input custom lunar coordinates across any Earth date and 29.5-day lunar cycle.
To address the challenge of assessing surface feasibility, our tool combines a 2D lunar terminator map with a real-time local sky horizon view that tracks Sun and Earth elevation angles, azimuths, and countdowns to sunset and Earthset. It automatically calculates solar power generation efficiency and direct Earth line-of-sight communication windows, presenting side-by-side trade-offs alongside a toggle between a technical Mission Engineer mode and a simplified Public/Educator mode.
This tool is important because lunar surface operations depend heavily on harsh illumination cycles, power constraints, and communication blackouts. By turning complex lunar ephemeris data into clear visual timelines and actionable metrics, Lunar Horizon helps mission planners optimize schedules while making lunar exploration engineering accessible to students and the public.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Lunar Horizon (Lunar Landing Navigator) is an interactive web tool that evaluates solar power and Earth communication feasibility for lunar missions. Users can compare key landing sites—Shackleton Crater Rim, Mare Tranquillitatis, and Tycho Crater—or input custom lunar coordinates across any Earth date and 29.53-day lunar cycle.

Key Features, Creativity & Impact

• Synchronized Visualizations: Pairs a 2D global lunar terminator map with a real-time local sky horizon dome tracking Sun and Earth positions.

• Mission Telemetry & Trade-Offs: Computes solar elevation, power generation efficiency, sunset/Earthset countdowns, and a live 3-site comparison matrix.

• Dual-Mode Accessibility: Includes a Mission Engineer Mode for technical planning and a Public / Educator Mode for STEM learning.
